bug_description.normalized: The staged reproducing checkout is ancestor `f905fa80d71d6a0f6d773938f39e3f9d7558d537`, not the metadata commit `f7b91535da39550693214dbe7ae2c16d83d70a4f`, but both contain the same vulnerable `src/bin/fuzz/template_fuzzer.cc` lines 57-63. The staged witness file is exactly 32768 bytes, so in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` the guard `if (size > sizeof(copy))` does not clamp `size`: the equality case leaves `size == 32768`. `memcpy(copy, data, size)` then fills the 32768-byte global `copy` buffer completely, and the next statement `copy[size] = '\0';` writes one byte at `copy[32768]`, immediately past the array. The saved ASan trace reports `global-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at line 63 and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of global `copy` defined at line 57. The patch expresses the missing obligation by clamping with `min(sizeof(copy) - 1, size)`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled input length and decides whether it is reduced to fit the fixed `copy` buffer.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_18988/poc` is exactly 32768 bytes (sha256 `699c00bfdc102d3c77b7d510e8b63ace6b123f3d31ed1f8afb918812252e1f60`). At this statement the exact equality case `size == sizeof(copy)` leaves `size` unchanged at 32768, which later becomes both the copy length and the terminator index.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The code uses the unchecked length as an array index into the 32768-byte global `copy` buffer and writes the terminating NUL one byte past the array.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `global-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `template_fuzzer.cc:63:16` and states that the address is 0 bytes to the right of global variable `copy` defined at line 57.

root_cause.description: The harness uses `>` instead of `>=`, so the exact-capacity input length is treated as safe even though the next statement always appends a NUL terminator.
root_cause.note: For the witnessed 32768-byte file, the guard is false and leaves `size` equal to the full array length. The patch fixes this exact off-by-one condition by clamping with `min(sizeof(copy) - 1, size)` before the copy and terminator write.

tainted_value_origin.description: The only attacker-controlled state needed on the crashing path is the libFuzzer-supplied length. The staged PoC is exactly 32768 bytes, and the crash happens before `lwan_tpl_compile_string_full()` reads the copied template contents.

parser_admitted.description: There is no deeper parser gate on the crashing path. The exact 32768-byte witness reaches the unsafe write because `size > sizeof(copy)` evaluates false at equality, so control falls through to the full-size copy and the terminator store.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness interprets the 32768-byte witness length with `if (size > sizeof(copy))`; because the guard uses `>` rather than `>=`, the equality case leaves `size` unchanged at the full buffer size.
`memcpy(copy, data, size)` fills the 32768-byte global `copy` array completely, and the following `copy[size] = '\0'` writes one byte at `copy[32768]`, matching the saved ASan global-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source and root cause. The staged PoC length is exactly 32768, equal to `sizeof(copy)`. Because the guard clamps only when `size > sizeof(copy)`, this equality case leaves `size` unchanged at 32768 instead of reducing it to 32767 before the later terminator write.
Uses the unchecked `size == 32768` from step 1 as the copy length. This fills `copy[0..32767]`, so the entire global buffer is occupied and no in-bounds slot remains for the trailing NUL.

Sink. The code reuses `size` as the terminator index. With `size == 32768` and valid elements only through `copy[32767]`, this stores a NUL at `copy[32768]`, the first byte past the global array. That matches the saved ASan `global-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at line 63 and the report that the address is 0 bytes to the right of global `copy` defined at line 57.

format.name: Exact-size template_fuzzer witness
format.contract: Any input of exactly 32768 bytes. The staged witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_18988/poc` is one such file (sha256 `699c00bfdc102d3c77b7d510e8b63ace6b123f3d31ed1f8afb918812252e1f60`). In the vulnerable source, only the equality case `size == sizeof(copy)` bypasses the clamp, so `memcpy` fills `copy[0..32767]` and the next statement `copy[size] = '\0';` writes one byte at `copy[32768]`. Shorter inputs leave room for the terminator, and longer inputs are clamped to 32767 before the write.
